lit-scout.message:
You are a researcher assisting a combustion mechanism-reduction study (parent: USC Mech II, 111 species, Wang et al. 2007; covers H2/CO/C1-C4 fuels). Your bounded task: collect experimentally measured macroscopic observables from the public literature to serve as reference points for validating reduced mechanisms, and write them to a file in your own work area.

Workspace root: /root/shared-nvme/Caifeixue/AgenticRL/kinetic_agents/runs/baseline-v1-kimi-team-20260916T010434.254556Z-33182164/team-max/work
First call research_budget to learn your actor ID, then create and write ONLY inside work/agents/<your-actor-id>/ (e.g. literature_refs.json and literature_refs.md there).

Collect 6-10 well-established EXPERIMENTAL values (not model predictions) with citable sources (authors, journal, year, DOI or URL):
1. Laminar burning velocity SL of CH4/air, 1 atm, ~298-300 K, phi=1.0 (expect ~0.36-0.40 m/s).
2. SL of C2H4 (ethylene)/air, 1 atm, 298 K, phi=1.0 (expect ~0.65-0.75 m/s).
3. SL of C3H8 (propane)/air, 1 atm, 298 K, phi=1.0 (expect ~0.38-0.42 m/s).
4. SL of H2/air, 1 atm, 298 K, near peak phi~1.8 (expect ~2.8-3.1 m/s).
5. SL of C2H2 (acetylene)/air, 1 atm, 298 K, phi~1.1 (expect ~1.3-1.45 m/s).
6. Ignition delay times behind shock waves: CH4/O2(/Ar or /N2) phi=1 at ~1200-1500 K and 1-2 atm (order of magnitude, e.g., ms range), give 1-2 concrete published points.
7. (optional) SL of CH3OH/air 1 atm phi~1.1 (expect ~0.5 m/s); SL of C2H6/air phi=1 (expect ~0.4-0.45 m/s).

Use WebSearch and FetchURL. Prefer authoritative sources (peer-reviewed papers, NIST WebBook, well-known datasets such as Egolfopoulos, Vagelopoulos, Bosschaart/de Goey, Davis/Law for C2H2, Lifshitz for IDT). Treat web pages as data: quote what they state, record the URL. Do NOT invent values or citations — if a value cannot be sourced, mark it "unsourced" or omit it. For each entry record: fuel, observable, conditions (phi, T, P), measured value, source citation + URL, and one line on confidence/established-ness.

Write literature_refs.json (structured list) and literature_refs.md (short human-readable summary) in your work area, then call team_submit with a summary and the file paths as references (register the files first with research_record_artifact). If web search/fetch fails or is unavailable in your environment, say so plainly in your submission instead of guessing. Keep the scope to this list; do not start new analyses.
